LESSON: WRITING WRITING

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing WRITING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing WRITING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: where they turn pages from right to left as books when writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently
2. use correct words and sentences for the grade level
3. give examples from school and home conversations
4. check your work for clarity and neatness

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING WRITING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing WRITING helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing WRITING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use correct words and sentences for the grade level

What this means
In this part you learn to use correct words and sentences for the grade level. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing WRITING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use correct words and sentences for the grade level. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Give examples from school and home conversations

What this means
In this part you learn to give examples from school and home conversations. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give examples from school and home conversations.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give examples from school and home conversations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Check your work for clarity and neatness

What this means
In this part you learn to check your work for clarity and neatness. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: check your work for clarity and neatness.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing WRITING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can check your work for clarity and neatness. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing WRITING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing WRITING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing WRITING to a partner. (skill: use correct words and sentences for the grade level)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: give examples from school and home conversations)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Writing WRITING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: check your work for clarity and neatness)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing WRITING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently.
3. Practise this skill: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.
4. Practise this skill: give examples from school and home conversations.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing WRITING from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing WRITING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Writing WRITING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. where they turn pages from right to left as books when writing?
2. Where do we place our (2HRS) a) Hold a writing tool • Learners could be guided to write patterns hands when writing?
3. How do we position our class. • Learners could be guided in activities on hands while writing?
4. How do we hold the writing to left during a writing between the index finger and the thumb, tool when writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing WRITING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: practise Writing WRITING clearly and confidently.
5. Be able to: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
